network.overall_strategy: The network is built around the experimentally well-supported pyruvate hub. Pyruvate is generated by three hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation variants distinguished by mineral assemblage and by two oxaloacetate decarboxylation routes, then converted to alanine either by a balanced net Fe-promoted reductive amination or by a more explicit, partly speculative oxime-mediated sequence. Two orthogonal direct entries bypass pyruvate entirely: surface hydrolysis of alanine aminonitrile and hydrothermal reduction of serine. Ten distinct pathways are enumerated. Because none of the cited routes is intrinsically enantioselective, the network is best read as producing an alanine pool that contains the requested L-alanine, with later L-enrichment unresolved. The weaker lactate-oxidation branch from the review is omitted here because the explicit oxidant/byproduct bookkeeping is underspecified in the curated report, whereas every reaction below is kept atom-balanced.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal CO2 fixation to pyruvate on Fe0-awaruite

conditions.other: anoxic, alkaline, H2-rich serpentinization-driven vent fluids

reactions.mechanism: Surface-mediated H2 activation and stepwise CO2 reduction with C-C bond formation on Fe-Ni alloy and iron metal surfaces.
reactions.reasoning: Preiner et al. (2020) experimentally obtained pyruvate from CO2 and H2 on Fe0/awaruite at 373 K. This node is encoded in conserved form as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O. It provides a purely geochemical entry into the pyruvate hub; the main limitation is pyruvate thermal lability, so cooler vent mixing zones are more plausible than the hottest effluents (Preiner et al., 2020).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal CO2 fixation to pyruvate on Fe0-magnetite

conditions.other: anoxic, alkaline, H2-rich vent fluids with mixed metal/oxide surfaces

reactions.mechanism: Fe0 supplies a highly reducing surface while magnetite adsorbs and activates CO2, enabling sequential reduction and C-C coupling to C3 products.
reactions.reasoning: Preiner et al. (2020) reported pyruvate formation from CO2 and H2 with Fe0 plus magnetite at 373 K. The present node uses the atom-balanced net stoichiometry 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O. This is a strong hydrothermal route because both minerals are geochemically plausible in serpentinizing systems, though pyruvate stability still limits the hottest settings (Preiner et al., 2020).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal CO2 fixation to pyruvate on magnetite alone

conditions.other: anoxic, H2-rich hydrothermal water contacting mixed-valence iron oxide surfaces

reactions.mechanism: CO2 adsorption and reduction on a mixed-valence iron oxide surface with subsequent carbon-carbon coupling to the C3 alpha-keto acid.
reactions.reasoning: Preiner et al. (2020) also observed pyruvate from CO2 and H2 on magnetite alone. The node is written as the conserved net reaction 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O. Magnetite-only chemistry is especially attractive geologically because the mineral is widespread, although it is generally less reducing than native metal/alloy systems and still faces the pyruvate-stability constraint (Preiner et al., 2020).

reactions.name: Fe2+-promoted hydrothermal decarboxylation of oxaloacetate
reactions.mechanism: Fe2+ coordinates the beta-keto dicarboxylate and lowers the barrier for beta-decarboxylation to pyruvate and CO2.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) showed Fe2+-promoted oxaloacetate decarboxylation in an iron-driven protometabolic network. Writing CO2 explicitly gives the conserved transformation oxaloacetate -> pyruvate + CO2. This route is chemically strong because beta-keto acid decarboxylation is intrinsically favorable at mild hydrothermal temperature (Muchowska et al., 2019).

reactions.name: Surface cyanosulfidic decarboxylation of oxaloacetate

conditions.other: cyanosulfidic surface pools with UV-dark cycling and episodic concentration

reactions.mechanism: Nonenzymatic beta-decarboxylation of oxaloacetate under cyanosulfidic surface conditions.
reactions.reasoning: Ritson (2021) reported oxaloacetate decarboxylation to pyruvate under surface cyanosulfidic conditions. The present network writes CO2 explicitly for atom conservation. This route usefully links surface photoredox chemistry to the pyruvate hub, although any downstream alanine formation from surface-generated pyruvate requires later concentration or transfer into Fe-rich settings (Ritson, 2021).

reactions.name: Balanced net hydrothermal reductive amination of pyruvate

conditions.other: anoxic, Fe-rich, H2-bearing hydrothermal microcompartments; local concentration on mineral surfaces mitigates dilution

reactions.mechanism: Hydroxylamine-derived imine/oxime formation at the alpha-keto group followed by Fe-assisted reduction to the amino acid.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019) experimentally showed Fe0/Fe2+-promoted conversion of pyruvate plus hydroxylamine to alanine at 343 K. To make the node atom-conserving, it is encoded here as the net hydrothermal reduction pyruvate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> alanine + 2 H2O, with Fe0/Fe2+ retained as mineral redox promoters and vent H2 used as the explicit source of reducing equivalents. This bookkeeping correction is chemically reasonable in H2-rich serpentinizing systems but more interpretive than the exact laboratory formulation; hydroxylamine availability remains debated, and no L-selectivity is demonstrated (Muchowska et al., 2019; Preiner et al., 2020).

reactions.name: Formation of pyruvate oxime from pyruvate and hydroxylamine

conditions.other: anoxic hydrothermal microfilms or pores where local concentration favors dehydration

reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of hydroxylamine to the keto carbonyl followed by dehydration to the oxime.
reactions.reasoning: This step is speculative but chemically justified. Hydroxylamine normally condenses with alpha-keto acids to give oximes plus water, and such intermediacy is the clearest balanced decomposition of the pyruvate-to-alanine chemistry reported by Muchowska et al. (2019). The provided alanine-specific studies did not directly isolate pyruvate oxime, so this node is included as a mechanistic surrogate rather than a directly demonstrated prebiotic transformation.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal reduction of pyruvate oxime to alanine

conditions.other: H2-rich hydrothermal water contacting Fe-rich mineral surfaces

reactions.mechanism: Reductive hydrogenation and deoxygenation of the oxime functionality to the amino acid with water release.
reactions.reasoning: This step is also speculative but chemically reasonable. Reduction of an oxime-like intermediate to an amino acid is a plausible H2/Fe-driven follow-up step in hydrothermal systems, connecting the oxime node back to the experimentally observed Fe-promoted alanine formation of Muchowska et al. (2019) and the H2-activating mineral context of Preiner et al. (2020). It is less directly supported than rxn_006 and likewise does not resolve chirality.

reactions.name: Surface hydrolysis of alanine aminonitrile

conditions.other: wet phases of cyanosulfidic evaporitic pools after aminonitrile accumulation; hydrolysis favored during UV-shielded or dark intervals

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration through amide-like intermediates to the carboxylic acid with ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support alanine formation by hydrolysis of 2-aminopropanenitrile in cyanosulfidic surface chemistry. The balanced encoding is 2-aminopropanenitrile + 2 H2O -> alanine + NH3. This is one of the clearest direct prebiotic routes to alanine, although aminonitrile persistence under strong UV and the lack of enantioselectivity remain open issues (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal reductive dehydroxylation of serine to alanine

conditions.other: submarine hydrothermal water with serpentinization-derived H2

reactions.mechanism: Reductive dehydroxylation of the side-chain hydroxymethyl group to a methyl group with water loss.
reactions.reasoning: Aubrey, Cleaves, and Bada (2008) reported hydrothermal conversion of serine to alanine; the conserved form is serine + H2 -> alanine + H2O. This route is experimentally grounded and geochemically plausible in H2-rich submarine systems, but it depends on prior serine availability and still gives no demonstrated route to L-enrichment (Aubrey et al., 2008).

pathways.name: Fe0-awaruite vent fixation plus direct net amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation on Fe0-awaruite forms pyruvate, followed by balanced Fe-promoted reductive amination to alanine.

pathways.name: Fe0-magnetite vent fixation plus direct net amination
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation on Fe0-magnetite forms pyruvate, then pyruvate undergoes balanced reductive amination to alanine.

pathways.name: Magnetite-only vent fixation plus direct net amination
pathways.description: Magnetite alone generates pyruvate from CO2/H2 hydrothermally, followed by direct balanced alanine-forming reductive amination.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal oxaloacetate decarboxylation plus direct net amination
pathways.description: Fe2+-promoted hydrothermal decarboxylation of oxaloacetate gives pyruvate, which then undergoes balanced reductive amination to alanine.

pathways.name: Surface oxaloacetate decarboxylation plus hydrothermal amination
pathways.description: Surface cyanosulfidic decarboxylation of oxaloacetate generates pyruvate, which is then transferred or concentrated into Fe-rich hydrothermal settings for reductive amination to alanine.

pathways.name: Fe0-awaruite vent fixation plus oxime route
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation on Fe0-awaruite gives pyruvate, then a speculative but chemically motivated oxime intermediate is formed and reduced to alanine.

pathways.name: Fe0-magnetite vent fixation plus oxime route
pathways.description: Hydrothermal CO2/H2 fixation on Fe0-magnetite feeds pyruvate into the oxime-mediated alanine-forming sequence.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal oxaloacetate decarboxylation plus oxime route
pathways.description: Fe2+-promoted hydrothermal decarboxylation of oxaloacetate supplies pyruvate, which proceeds through the speculative oxime intermediate to alanine.

pathways.name: Direct surface aminonitrile hydrolysis
pathways.description: Alanine aminonitrile hydrolyzes directly in cyanosulfidic surface waters to alanine with ammonia release.

pathways.name: Direct hydrothermal serine reduction
pathways.description: Serine is reduced under H2-rich hydrothermal conditions to alanine by reductive dehydroxylation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong hydrothermal route assembled from experimentally supported CO2 fixation and pyruvate amination chemistry. The main limitation is that rxn_006 is represented as a net H2 reduction rather than an explicitly Fe0/Fe2+-promoted step, and the endpoint is alanine with unresolved stereochemistry rather than a defined L-only product.
suggestions: Write rxn_001 explicitly as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O.
State Fe0/Fe2+ and mild hydrothermal conditions for rxn_006, not just the net H2 stoichiometry.
Add an enantioenrichment step or relabel the endpoint as alanine rather than resolved L-alanine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically sound hydrothermal route using a literature-supported Fe0-magnetite fixation variant feeding the iron-driven pyruvate-to-alanine transformation. As in P1, rxn_006 needs clearer Fe0/Fe2+ catalytic context, and stereochemistry remains unresolved at the target node.
suggestions: Write rxn_002 explicitly as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O.
Annotate rxn_006 with Fe0/Fe2+, ~70 C hydrothermal conditions, and the full net stoichiometry.
Clarify that the route produces alanine without demonstrated L-selectivity.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Credible and literature-backed, but the magnetite-only fixation branch is usually less robust than Fe0-containing variants and still depends on the same under-specified net amination step rxn_006. The chemistry reaches alanine, but not a defined L-enriched endpoint.
suggestions: Write rxn_003 explicitly as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O.
Specify the exact magnetite-only hydrothermal conditions and note that this variant is weaker than Fe0-containing systems.
Add explicit Fe0/Fe2+ context for rxn_006 and clarify the stereochemical limitation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: One of the most internally coherent hub pathways: hydrothermal Fe2+-promoted oxaloacetate decarboxylation feeds a literature-supported iron-driven pyruvate-to-alanine step in the same broad setting. The remaining weaknesses are the net treatment of rxn_006 and the lack of a true L-selective endpoint.
suggestions: Annotate rxn_004 with Fe2+ and the mild hydrothermal temperature window used experimentally.
Annotate rxn_006 with Fe0/Fe2+ and its full net stoichiometry: pyruvate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> alanine + 2 H2O.
If L-alanine is the required endpoint, add a stereochemical enrichment or selection step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable hybrid route, but pyruvate movement from a surface cyanosulfidic setting to a hydrothermal iron-amination setting is assumed rather than represented. rxn_005 would benefit from more explicit cyanosulfidic conditions, and the alanine product remains stereochemically unresolved.
suggestions: Add an explicit transport or concentration step justifying pyruvate transfer from surface pools to hydrothermal settings.
Specify the cyanosulfidic reagents and conditions for rxn_005 rather than labeling it only as Surface.
State Fe0/Fe2+ conditions for rxn_006 and clarify that the endpoint is alanine without demonstrated L-enrichment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Oxime formation is plausible, but the pathway becomes speculative at rxn_008: reducing pyruvate oxime to alanine with H2 under generic hydrothermal conditions is not directly established here without a realistic mineral hydrogenation context. Treat this as a hypothesis rather than a literature-secure route.
suggestions: Provide direct experimental support for rxn_008 or replace the sequence with the literature-supported net reductive amination rxn_006.
Add a realistic Fe/Ni mineral catalyst context and write rxn_008 explicitly as pyruvate oxime + 2 H2 -> alanine + H2O.
Keep this branch explicitly labeled as speculative in the network summary.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This route inherits the same main weakness as P6: rxn_008 is not well supported as a standalone hydrothermal hydrogenation step under the stated conditions. The upstream fixation step is credible, but the downstream oxime reduction keeps the overall pathway below approval.
suggestions: Add direct literature support for oxime reduction under prebiotic hydrothermal conditions or remove this branch.
Specify a plausible Fe/Ni mineral hydrogenation catalyst for rxn_008 and include the full 2 H2 stoichiometry.
If retained, clearly separate the experimentally grounded and speculative portions of the pathway.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Coherent on paper, with a strong upstream oxaloacetate-to-pyruvate step, but the downstream oxime reduction remains the weak link. rxn_008 needs direct experimental support or a clearly stated Fe/Ni mineral catalyst system to be competitive with the literature-supported net amination route.
suggestions: Keep rxn_004 as the supported upstream step but replace rxn_007-rxn_008 with rxn_006 unless direct evidence for oxime reduction is added.
If rxn_008 is retained, specify the mineral catalyst and full stoichiometry explicitly.
State clearly that this branch is more speculative than the direct pyruvate amination pathways.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best-supported direct route in the network. Surface hydrolysis of alanine aminonitrile is literature-aligned and chemically straightforward; rxn_009 should explicitly consume 2 H2O, and stereochemistry remains unresolved at network level.
suggestions: Write rxn_009 explicitly as alanine aminonitrile + 2 H2O -> alanine + NH3.
Specify the aqueous or wet-dry cyanosulfidic conditions used for the hydrolysis step.
If true L-alanine is required, define a chiral aminonitrile precursor or add an enantioenrichment step.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Literature-supported single-step entry, but the reductive dehydroxylation of serine is less mechanistically specified here than the pyruvate routes and would benefit from clearer vent mineral context. It reaches alanine, but not a resolved L-only product as written.
suggestions: Specify the hydrothermal temperature, pressure, and any mineral catalyst or surface associated with rxn_010.
Clarify whether mol_009 is intended to be L-serine; if so, encode stereochemistry consistently.
Discuss competing hydrothermal serine decomposition pathways so the alanine-yield claim is better bounded.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected, internally consistent, literature-aligned network with a sensible pyruvate-hub strategy and no RDKit-detected conservation violations. For clarity, rxn_001-rxn_003 should be written as 3 CO2 + 5 H2 -> pyruvate + 3 H2O, rxn_006 as pyruvate + hydroxylamine + 2 H2 -> alanine + 2 H2O, rxn_008 as pyruvate oxime + 2 H2 -> alanine + H2O, and rxn_009 as alanine aminonitrile + 2 H2O -> alanine + NH3. The strongest chemistry is P9 directly and P4 among hub-based routes; the main reasons the network stays below the 0.9 approval threshold are the under-specified Fe0/Fe2+ context for rxn_006, the speculative nature of rxn_008, the unmodeled surface-to-hydrothermal transfer in P5, and unresolved stereochemistry because mol_010 is formula-only and the network reaches alanine pools rather than a defined L-alanine endpoint. Omitting the underspecified lactate branch was a reasonable choice.
